_README: HELD-OUT route/menu corpus. Frozen 2026-08-02, BEFORE any of the routing
fixes the v1.108.217 counterfactual recommended were written.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The catalog moratorium (v1.108.219) gated its exit on
route@1 measured against queries.json -- the same corpus whose misses were
about to be fixed. Fitting rules to a corpus and then scoring on it measures
memorisation, not routing. The deep-research report said 'held-out,
low-leakage corpus' and that word was dropped when the gate was written.
This corpus restores it.
CONSTRUCTION, and the order is the whole point:
1. Every entry here was written BEFORE the first rule or description edit.
2. For each intent the counterfactual named as defective, this file holds
ONE OR MORE ALTERNATE PHRASINGS of the same user intent. That is the
discriminating test: a rule that only matches the phrasing in
queries.json will pass there and fail here, and the gap between the two
numbers is the amount of overfitting.
3. Control entries cover intents that were NOT defective, so a fix that
breaks a working route shows up as a regression rather than hiding
inside an improved aggregate.
LEAKAGE DISCIPLINE is inherited from queries.json verbatim: phrased as the
task a user actually has, in the user's vocabulary, without the target
action's name or description in view. The harness scores leakage per query
here too.
AUTHOR CONTAMINATION, stated rather than hidden. The author of this file had
already seen which actions were missing when writing it. That cannot be
undone, and it is why the entries are alternate PHRASINGS of intents rather
than a re-pick of which intents to test: the choice of what to measure is
contaminated, the choice of how a user words it is much less so. A corpus
written by someone who has never seen explanations.json would be better and
is worth soliciting.
This file is NOT edited to make a number move. Same rule as queries.json.
